note: Where MABAYANI came from, stated on the page itself. This is hand-authored and lives apart from data/mabayani.json, which scripts/parse-mabayani-spec.py regenerates wholesale from the brief — anything added there by hand is lost on the next parse.
rules: Every word of this block is the project's own, supplied for this page. Nothing here is written for the author or paraphrased from her.

`epigraphSource` says where the quoted line came from and the build refuses to run without it. "quotation-card" means the line must appear word for word inside the closing card in data/mabayani-assets.json, and scripts/build-mabayani.py checks that it does. "supplied" means the project provided it directly as the author's own message; a machine cannot verify that, so the declaration is the record of who vouched for it. A line with no declared source does not ship.

Her name appears on this page and in the closing reflection of bulletin/why-mabayani-exists.html, and nowhere else on the site. scripts/check-mabayani-anonymity.py enforces that against the built HTML.
The portrait is hers, supplied by her. It is shown at the size a portrait is shown at and never treated as decoration or as a background.
No publication date, publisher or way to buy the book is stated, because none has been given. The About Masinloc band carries the note that it is being prepared for publication.
author: Binibining Francine Marie Bautista
label: Where this comes from
title: MABAYANI began as a book.
body: Researched and written by Binibining Francine Marie Bautista, it was donated to this initiative to help make Masinloc’s history more accessible.
If you loved this section, you’ll love the book even more.
epigraph: To be a MABAYANI is to remember, protect, question, and carry our history forward.
